title: Jerry Tubbs: OU Center Turned Cowboys Assistant Coach
question: What did Oklahoma center Jerry Tubbs do after his playing days at OU?
answer: Jerry Tubbs, who played at Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956, went on to play linebacker in the NFL from 1957 to 1967 and then served on the Dallas Cowboys' coaching staff for more than two decades.
summary: Jerry Tubbs starred for Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956, won the Walter Camp Award, played in the NFL, then spent over 20 years as a Dallas Cowboys assistant.
body: Jerry Tubbs played for Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956, and in those three varsity seasons the Sooners never lost, going 31-0 under Bud Wilkinson. He began as a fullback, then settled in at center in 1955, and he also played linebacker, which made him a two-way force for the 1955 and 1956 national championship teams.

His college résumé was crowded. He was a unanimous All-American in 1956, finished fourth in that year's Heisman Trophy voting, and became the first Sooner to receive the Walter Camp Award as the nation's top player. The National Football Foundation inducted him into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1996.

After graduating, Tubbs took his talents to the NFL. He played linebacker from 1957 through 1967 for the Chicago Cardinals, the San Francisco 49ers and the Dallas Cowboys, finishing his playing days in Dallas.

He did not leave the Cowboys when he stopped playing. Tubbs moved onto the coaching staff and stayed as an assistant for more than two decades, working under head coach Tom Landry. Published accounts give slightly different totals, so we describe it simply as over twenty years.

Tubbs died in June 2012 at the age of 77, and the University of Oklahoma announced his passing. For Sooner fans he remains a reminder of how the Wilkinson-era stars carried their football careers well beyond Norman.
